newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed (mixed to) slightly higher on Tuesday, shrugging off corrections on surrounding bond markets and strong U.S. economic data.
Market attention focused on tap sales of the ten-year 5.75 percent state loan issued in January, which was reopened today.
Dealers said the Dutch Finance Ministry seemed to have done some good business in the loan in the early session, but they were divided over the number of parties involved.
"There has been a lot of trade in that bond since it was announced last Friday already," one dealer said.

Market players rushed onto the market trying to buy the bond at this morning's first issue price of 99.35, but the Dutch Finance Ministry's capital markets agency raised the price to 99.50 within minutes.
"There were quite some shorts that had to be covered, and it was nicely priced at the start as well," another dealer said.
After twenty minutes of trade, the state raised its price to 99.55 and kept it there until the close of today's sales.
Dealers said Dutch bond prices were supported by market players buying the benchmark and surrounding maturities in order to cover their short positions.
At the end of trade, the state said it had collected 1.9 billion guilders under the tap issue today.
Dealers had said they estimated the amount sold under the tap issue today to be somewhere above two billion guiders.

Most market players expect the state to collect between five and 7.5 billion guilders under this second tranche, increasing the amount on issue in the 10-year benchmark state loan to between 12.5 billion and 15.0 billion.
On May 14, the Finance Ministry said that only 10.0 billion guilders of its 1997 borrowing requirement remained.
Sales in the tap issue will continue from 0700 GMT to 1500 GMT each day until further notice.
"Once they (the state) have closed this loan, there'll be a short term shortage in Dutch government paper, which might drive prices higher," one dealer said.
Another added the Dutch bond market could well outperform Germany if the state paper had been placed with end-investors.
"But I have the impression tap sales are rather position-driven than order-driven at the moment," he said.
"And, although the Dutch economy performs fine, we might well feel the impact of EMU worries later on as well."
